title: CycloneDX SBOM for every published module, generated only for a -Prelease run
requirement: The release build shall generate a CycloneDX SBOM for each of the nine published modules when run with `./gradlew -Prelease releaseSbom`, through the CycloneDX Gradle plugin that the root `build.gradle` applies only inside `if (project.hasProperty('release'))` by `apply from: 'gradle/release.gradle'`, so that a default `./gradlew build`, online or offline, never resolves the plugin and no release task is wired into `check` or `build`.
rationale: Covers D-375, wave decision Release plugins (r4 W2-004), I-019 and T50. Measured (2026-10-20): the nine published modules are the entries of `naruModules` in `build.gradle:11-12`; the Gradle plugin portal metadata lists `org.cyclonedx:cyclonedx-gradle-plugin` up to 3.5.1 and the network was reachable; `build.gradle` has a `plugins {}` block with `ru.vyarus.animalsniffer` and the Kotlin plugin `apply false`. Decision: the plugin is applied from `gradle/release.gradle`, a script plugin with its own `buildscript {}` block, because a `plugins {}` block cannot be conditional and resolves its plugin even with `apply false`; `gradle/release.gradle` is not a module build file, so CON-BUILD-003 AC-2 (no `build.gradle` in a module directory) holds and AC-1 (the root `build.gradle` holds the plugin, compile, dependency and check configuration of every module) holds for every module configuration, only release-only tasks live in the applied script. The plugin version is an exact literal pinned when the file is written (not a dynamic range); the SBOM files go to `build/reports/naruserve/sbom/<module>.cdx.json`; the lifecycle task names are `releaseSbom`, `releaseScan`, `releaseLicenses` and `releaseCheck`. Pitfall: `BuildLayoutTest` reads `build.gradle` for pinned strings (`'java-library'`, `options.release = 8`, the class-reference prefixes), so the conditional apply is added without touching them. Rejected alternative: a `buildscript { classpath }` in the root file; it resolves the plugin on every build, including offline.
acceptanceCriteria: `./gradlew -Prelease releaseSbom` writes one CycloneDX JSON file per published module — nine files named `<module>.cdx.json` under `build/reports/naruserve/sbom/`, one for each entry of `naruModules` — each with `bomFormat` `CycloneDX` and a component for every `runtimeClasspath` dependency of that module (Gson 2.14.0 for `NaruServe-gson`, `kotlin-stdlib` for `NaruServe-kotlin`, `slf4j-api` for `NaruServe-slf4j`, the TinyHttpd components for `NaruServe-tinyhttpd`), and none for `compileOnly` or test-scope artifacts (the Servlet API and Jetty). [D-375; T50]
The run is recorded with its command, date, file list and component counts in `docs/release/test-results.md` under T50, because the plugin cannot be resolved by the default build. [D-375; D-381]

A default-build test asserts that `build.gradle` contains the conditional `apply from: 'gradle/release.gradle'` guarded by `project.hasProperty('release')`, that the strings `cyclonedx` and `dependencycheck` occur in no file of the root build except `gradle/release.gradle`, that `gradle/release.gradle` pins each plugin version as an exact literal, and that no release task is a dependency of `check`, `build` or `test`. [r4 W2-004; I-019]
`./gradlew build --offline` with a Gradle user home that holds neither plugin succeeds, which a recorded run (command, date, exit code) shows for the release machine. [r4 W2-004; I-019]

The default `./gradlew build` still passes `BuildLayoutTest` unchanged, including `con_BUILD_003_AC1_rootBuildFileHoldsPluginsCompileDependenciesAndChecks` and `con_BUILD_003_AC2_noModuleBuildFile`. [CON-BUILD-003]

title: Dependency vulnerability scan with a pending record that keeps the full dependency list
requirement: The release build shall run `./gradlew -Prelease releaseScan`, an OWASP Dependency-Check scan of the runtime dependencies of the published modules, and write `build/reports/naruserve/vulnerability-scan.md` with the status `completed` and the findings, or, whenever the scanner cannot finish — no network, a missing NVD API key, a rate limit or a tool error — with the status `pending`, the failure reason and the full dependency list (`group:name:version`, one line each, sorted, without duplicates), without failing the build for that reason.
rationale: Covers D-376, wave decision Release scan and result rows (r3 W2-005: pending for any reason the scanner cannot finish) and T50; the block on findings is FR-REL-003. Measured (2026-10-20): the Gradle plugin portal lists `org.owasp:dependency-check-gradle` up to 13.0.0; the network was reachable but a scan without an NVD API key is rate-limited and can fail partway; the shipped runtime dependencies are Gson 2.14.0, `kotlin-stdlib` with its `org.jetbrains:annotations`, `slf4j-api` 1.7.36 and the TinyHttpd components (`build.gradle:52-62`). Decision: the committed record of the release run is `docs/release/vulnerability-scan.md`, copied from the build report; the scan covers the `runtimeClasspath` of the nine published modules and excludes test scope (Jetty 9.4 of the Servlet tests); the scanner's own failure is caught by a wrapper task that writes the pending report. Pitfall: Dependency-Check fails the build on an update error by default; the wrapper converts that into `pending`, otherwise an offline release machine could not record anything. Rejected alternative: treating a pending scan as a pass; the record says `pending`, T50 stays `manual-pending` for this part and I-020 forbids promoting a requirement on a pending check.
acceptanceCriteria: With the scanner stubbed to fail for each of four causes — no network, a missing NVD API key, a rate limit and a tool error — the report writer produces a report whose status line is `pending`, whose reason line names the cause, and whose dependency list equals the sorted union of the `group:name:version` of the `runtimeClasspath` of the nine published modules, which an automated test over the writer function asserts without network. [D-376; r3 W2-005]

A finished scan produces the status `completed` with a findings table (dependency, identifier, CVSS score, severity), or the sentence `no findings`, and the report names the scanner version and the data timestamp. [D-376]

`docs/release/vulnerability-scan.md` exists and holds the report of the release run (`pending` with the reason, or `completed`), and the T50 vulnerability line of `docs/release/test-results.md` is `manual-pending` when the report is `pending` and `automated` or `verified` when it is `completed`, which a docs test compares. [D-376; D-381]
The report's dependency list excludes `compileOnly` and test-scope artifacts (the Servlet API, JSpecify, JUnit, Jetty) and includes the TinyHttpd components. [D-376]

title: Release is blocked by an unexcepted High or Critical dependency vulnerability
requirement: The release build shall fail `releaseCheck` while the vulnerability report shows a High or Critical finding (CVSS 7.0 or higher) for a runtime dependency of a published module that has no recorded exception in `docs/release/vulnerability-exceptions.md`, where an exception names the vulnerability id, the dependency, the reason, the approver and the date; a `pending` scan does not block the build but is shown as pending, never as passed.
rationale: Covers D-377, I-019 and I-020, wave decision Release scan and result rows (r3 W2-005: a finished scan with a High or Critical finding still blocks) and T50. Measured: `object.md:1170` (the first general release gate) requires "no unresolved High/Critical dependency vulnerability (exception approval procedure separate)". Decision: severity follows the CVSS v3 base score (High 7.0 to 8.9, Critical 9.0 and above), an exception row with a missing field counts as no exception, the exceptions file starts with a header and the line `no exceptions`, and a `pending` report is shown in the release notes as an open item. Pitfall: a `pending` status must not read as green; the release documentation and `docs/release/test-results.md` print the literal. Rejected alternative: blocking while the scan is pending; D-376 makes pending an allowed recorded state for an offline run, and blocking it would make an offline release impossible, so the open item is explicit instead.
acceptanceCriteria: A fixture report with one High finding and no exception makes the check fail with a message naming the vulnerability id and the dependency; the same report with a complete exception row passes; a Medium finding passes; a Critical finding fails; an exception row without a reason or approver is ignored and the check still fails. [D-377]

A fixture report with the status `pending` makes the check pass and prints `scan pending: release not cleared for T50 vulnerability part`, and the release notes list the scan as pending. [D-377; r3 W2-005]
`docs/release/vulnerability-exceptions.md` exists with the table header (id, dependency, reason, approver, date) and either the recorded exceptions or `no exceptions`. [D-377]
The check reads only the runtime dependencies of the published modules, so a High finding in a test-scope artifact does not block, which a fixture asserts. [D-377]

title: License report: every shipped dependency is non-GPL and listed in THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md
requirement: The release build shall run `./gradlew releaseLicenses`, which resolves the license of every dependency on the `runtimeClasspath` of the published modules, fails when any has a GPL-family license (GPL, LGPL or AGPL) or none that can be determined, and writes `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` at the repository root listing each shipped dependency as `group:name:version` with its license name and URL, and a default-build test shall fail when that file does not list exactly those dependencies.
rationale: Covers D-378 and T50. Measured (2026-10-20): the root `LICENSE` and `/Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/LICENSE` both open "BSD 3-Clause License"; Gson, `kotlin-stdlib` and `org.jetbrains:annotations` are Apache-2.0 and `slf4j-api` 1.7.36 is MIT by their POMs; `javax.servlet-api` 3.1.0 (CDDL with GPLv2 classpath exception) is `compileOnly` and therefore provided by the container, not shipped; `build.gradle` already writes the resolved graphs to `build/reports/naruserve/dependency-graphs.txt` (`checkDependencyRules`). Decision: licenses come from the POMs through an artifact resolution query; the TinyHttpd components come from an override table in `gradle/release.gradle` with the source `TinyHttpd/LICENSE` (the included build has no POM); a component with no license information and no override fails the task; the file also lists the compile-only artifacts under "provided by the container or the build, not shipped" with their licenses so the CDDL/GPL entry is explicit. Pitfall: a dependency whose POM states two licenses (dual license) passes when at least one is non-GPL and the file lists both. Rejected alternative: a name-based allowlist of group ids; a new transitive dependency would pass unseen.
acceptanceCriteria: `releaseLicenses` writes `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` with one row per shipped dependency — Gson 2.14.0, `kotlin-stdlib` and its annotations artifact, `slf4j-api` 1.7.36 and the TinyHttpd components — giving license name and URL, and a section of provided artifacts that names `javax.servlet-api` as container-provided and not shipped. [D-378; T50]

The license check, exercised by an automated test over its decision function with fixtures, fails for GPL-2.0, LGPL-3.0 and AGPL-3.0 and for an unknown license, and passes for Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-3-Clause and a dual license with one non-GPL member. [D-378]

A default-build test compares the dependency list parsed from `build/reports/naruserve/dependency-graphs.txt` (the shipped runtime dependencies) with the rows of `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` and fails, naming the dependency, on a missing or extra row, so the committed file cannot go stale. [D-378; I-005]
The run of `releaseLicenses` on the release machine is recorded under T50 in `docs/release/test-results.md` with its command and result. [D-378; D-381]

title: Publishing the nine modules to mavenLocal with maven-publish from the root build
requirement: The root build shall publish each of the nine modules to `mavenLocal` with `maven-publish` configured in the root `build.gradle` — coordinates `com.snoworca.naruserve:<module>:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT`, no remote repository — with a POM whose dependencies carry the versions the resolved graph selects, including the TinyHttpd components of `NaruServe-tinyhttpd`.
rationale: Covers wave decision Publishing (r1 W2-004: v1 publishes to `mavenLocal` only, README coordinates `com.snoworca.naruserve:<module>:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT`, the POM mechanism is settled at SRS authoring) and D-383 (POM part), D-375, D-379. Measured (2026-10-20): `build.gradle` has no `maven-publish` and `allprojects` sets group `com.snoworca.naruserve` and version `0.1.0-SNAPSHOT`; the Gradle declaration of the TinyHttpd dependencies is versionless because "the included build substitutes the coordinates" (CON-BUILD-006); TinyHttpd's own build sets group `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd` and version `0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` and has no publishing configuration. Decision: `maven-publish` (a core Gradle plugin, so no download) with `versionMapping { allVariants { fromResolutionResult() } }`, which writes the resolved version of each declared dependency into the POM, so the POM of `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` names `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd:tinyhttpd-core:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` and `tinyhttpd-websocket:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT`; the Gradle declarations stay versionless and CON-BUILD-006 stays true. `api` dependencies become compile scope and `implementation` ones runtime scope. Pitfall: without the version mapping the generated POM has a dependency without a `<version>`, which Maven consumers reject. Rejected alternative: publishing sources and javadoc jars; v1 publishes to the local repository only, reopen with a remote repository.
acceptanceCriteria: `./gradlew publishToMavenLocal` installs, for each of the nine modules, a jar and a POM under `com/snoworca/naruserve/<module>/0.1.0-SNAPSHOT/` of the Maven local repository (a test uses a temporary `maven.repo.local`), without `-Prelease` and without network access beyond the existing dependencies. [wave decision Publishing]

A test generates the POM of every module and asserts: `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` declares `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd:tinyhttpd-core` and `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd:tinyhttpd-websocket` each with the non-empty version of the included build (`0.1.0-SNAPSHOT`), `NaruServe-gson` declares `com.google.code.gson:gson:2.14.0` in compile scope, `NaruServe-kotlin` declares `kotlin-stdlib` with `2.2.0`, `NaruServe-slf4j` declares `slf4j-api:1.7.36`, `NaruServe-servlet` declares `NaruServe-api` and no Servlet API, and `NaruServe` declares `NaruServe-tinyhttpd`, `NaruServe-gson` and `NaruServe-logcat` in runtime scope. [D-383]

`publishing.repositories` holds no remote repository, only the implicit `mavenLocal`, which a text test of `build.gradle` asserts; the Gradle declarations of the TinyHttpd dependencies stay versionless (CON-BUILD-006 unchanged). [wave decision Publishing; CON-BUILD-006]
`maven-publish` is applied in the root `build.gradle` itself, not in `gradle/release.gradle`, so `publishToMavenLocal` works in a default offline build. [r4 W2-004; I-019]

rationale: Covers D-379 and wave decisions Release documentation statement (r1 W1-005) and Publishing (r1 W2-004); supports T50 ("README, API documents and license list exist", the first general release gate at `object.md:1170`). Measured (2026-10-20): the repository root has no `README.md`; `docs/api/README.md:11-60` holds the "5분 시작" Java and Kotlin blocks and `:87-115` the module table with the nine coordinates and `0.1.0-SNAPSHOT`; `docs/api/README.md:6-7` still says the document is a target contract that is "아직 구현되지 않았습니다" (OPS-REL-002 rewrites it). [D-379; wave decision Publishing]

The ```java and ```kotlin quick-start blocks of `README.md` are character-for-character equal to the Java and Kotlin blocks under "5분 시작" of `docs/api/README.md`, which a docs test asserts, and the Java block is one of the blocks the root docs compile test compiles. [D-379; I-009]

`README.md` states that the Android sample build and API 21 device or emulator verification are not part of v1 and that API 21 compatibility rests on `--release 8` and the animal-sniffer `android-api-level-21` check, and links `docs/api/README.md`, `docs/release/release-notes.md`, `docs/release/test-results.md` and `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md`, all of which exist. title: Every (미확정) marker of docs/api is resolved or rewritten as a post-v1 item, with three recorded exceptions
requirement: The system shall leave in `docs/api/` no `(미확정)` marker except the three rows of `docs/api/express-migration.md` for `express.Router()`, `res.redirect(url)` and `cors()`, resolving every other marker or rewriting it as an explicit post-v1 item with its reason, and shall list the three kept rows in the release documentation as open Express-compatibility items for after v1.
rationale: Covers D-380, D-347 (post-v1 rewrite), wave decisions Status of the removed Android tests (r1 W1-001), Pinned heading (r2 W2-002) and Markers pinned by earlier tests (r4 W2-001), and I-013. Frozen: D-380 says every marker is resolved or rewritten. Deviation (recorded): the three express-migration rows keep their text because verified acceptance criteria pin them (`HttpDocsTest` via OPS-HTTP-007 AC-8, `AppDocsTest` via OPS-APP-005 AC-6, `WaveFiveDocsTest.kept`); the check allows exactly those three. Measured (2026-10-20, grep over `docs/api`): `servlet.md` six lines (OPS-SVL-001), `README.md:7` (the legend sentence), `response.md:141` (`res.redirect`), and `express-migration.md` lines 28, 72, 73, 74, 88 and 306 (`express.Router()`, `res.redirect(url)`, `res.type`, `res.render`, `cors()` and the undecided-section sentence). Wave 8 changes one verified assertion: OPS-HTTP-007 AC-8 pins that `response.md` keeps exactly one marker line for `res.redirect`; it is superseded by OPS-HTTP-008 and `HttpDocsTest.sdsAc6_OPS_HTTP_007_AC8_responseKeepsOnlyRedirectMarker` is re-pointed to assert zero marker lines in `response.md` and the post-v1 sentence. Kept unchanged: the heading "저사양 Android 튜닝(수동 후속 작업)" of `defaults.md` (OPS-APP-005 AC-4, `WaveSevenDocsTest`), the three `KEPT` rows of `AppDocsTest`, the `kept(...)` rows of `WaveFiveDocsTest`, and the `defaults.md` line with "TLS 리스너" and "v1" (`WaveFiveDocsTest:447`). Pitfall: the kept `res.redirect(url)` row and the rewritten `response.md` line say the same thing in two states; the rewritten line states that `res.redirect` is not in v1 and shows `res.status(302).header("Location", url).end()`, and the row keeps its marker only because a verified test pins it. Rejected alternative: removing the three markers and re-pointing three test classes; the wave decision keeps the verified assertions.
acceptanceCriteria: A docs test over `docs/api/*.md` finds `(미확정)` on exactly three lines, the rows starting with `| `express.Router()``, `| `res.redirect(url)`` and `| `cors()`` of `express-migration.md`, and on no other line. [D-380; r4 W2-001]

`docs/api/README.md` no longer says the document is not implemented or explains the marker: the status banner states that the document describes the v1 implementation and that the three Express-compatibility rows are the only open items, and the (미확정) legend sentence is gone. [D-380]

`response.md` holds no marker: the line on `res.redirect` states that `res.redirect` is not part of v1, why (no wave of the run owns it; Express-style helpers are out of the v1 scope), and the replacement `res.status(302).header("Location", url).end()`; the `express-migration.md` rows for `res.type('png')` and `res.render(view)` and the undecided-section sentence are rewritten as v1 exclusions with their reasons and carry no marker. [D-380; r4 W2-001]

`defaults.md` keeps the heading "저사양 Android 튜닝(수동 후속 작업)" unchanged and has directly under it a sentence stating that the tuning is a post-v1 item (not a manual-pending release check) because Android device verification is out of v1 scope, while the pinned `WaveSevenDocsTest` and OPS-APP-005 AC-4 assertions pass unchanged. [D-347; D-380; r2 W2-002]

`docs/release/release-notes.md` lists each post-v1 item with its reason: the three open Express-compatibility rows, `res.type`, `res.render`, the low-end Android tuning of D-347, TLS/WSS (OPS-REL-006), `suspend` handlers (OPS-KT-001), the `jakarta.servlet` module and WebSocket on the Servlet adapter. [D-380; D-347]
The tests that pinned a changed assertion are re-pointed: `HttpDocsTest` methods of OPS-HTTP-007 AC-8 to OPS-HTTP-008, and no other docs test changes its expectation. [D-380; I-013]

title: Release test results document listing T01 to T50 with four status literals and evidence links
requirement: The repository shall contain `docs/release/test-results.md`, which lists T01 to T50 of `object.md` §17.2 with one line each (two lines each for T26 and T49: the JVM part and the Android device part), gives each line exactly one status literal of `automated`, `manual-pending`, `verified` or `out-of-v1-scope` and an evidence link, marks T10, T12, T47 and the Android device parts of T26 and T49 `out-of-v1-scope` with the reason `user decision 2026-10-20`, and records the full-suite result of `./gradlew build`.
rationale: Covers D-381, I-018, I-019, I-020, D-347 (listed as a post-v1 row), T10, T12, T47, T26, T49 and T50, and wave decisions Status of the removed Android tests (r1 W1-001), Status literal (r2 W2-005) and Release scan and result rows (r3 W2-005). Frozen: D-381 names three statuses; Deviation (recorded): the fourth literal `out-of-v1-scope` is added and I-018 is narrowed for the five Android lines by the user's decision, which also supersedes the header wording "device parts of T26 and T49 recorded as manual checks" and the Q-3 manual device run; I-020 does not apply to them because they are not manual-pending, and no requirement may call them verified. Decision: `automated` means an automated test of `./gradlew build` covers it (evidence `path#method`), `manual-pending` a recorded manual check not yet run (evidence a checklist item), `verified` a manual check run with recorded evidence; the document and its test use the literal only, never the prose "out of v1 scope (user decision)". Measured: `object.md:1015-1082` holds the T-table and the platform matrix; T10, T12 and T47 read "Gson 2.14.0 API21 실기기", "R8 최적화 on" and "Android Service 메인스레드 IO 금지". Pitfall: a result document that lists a test as `automated` without a method link rots silently; the docs test resolves each link to an existing file and method. Rejected alternative: marking the Android tests `manual-pending` with a checklist; the user removed device verification from v1.
acceptanceCriteria: The document has one line for each of T01 to T50 and a second line for T26 and T49, so 52 lines in all, whose ids equal the ids of the §17.2 table of `object.md`, which a docs test parses from both files. [D-381; I-018]

Each line carries exactly one of the literals `automated`, `manual-pending`, `verified` and `out-of-v1-scope` and the test rejects any other status word; T10, T12, T47, the T26 device line and the T49 device line carry `out-of-v1-scope` with the reason `user decision 2026-10-20`, and no other line carries it. [D-381; r1 W1-001; r2 W2-005; r3 W2-005]

Each `automated` line links a test file that exists, and when the link has a `#method` part the method exists in that file; each `manual-pending` line links a checklist item of the document; each `verified` line links the recorded evidence; the T50 lines for the SBOM, the vulnerability scan (with its `pending` or `completed` literal of FR-REL-002) and the license check link their records. [D-381; I-018]

The document contains a post-v1 row for the low-end Android tuning of D-347 and records the date, command, commit and test count of the full-suite run of `./gradlew build` (I-019); no requirement is `verified` on the strength of a `manual-pending` line (I-020). [D-347; I-019; I-020]

title: Release notes platform matrix: Java 8 runtime row pending with compile-time evidence, Android rows out of v1 scope
requirement: The release documentation `docs/release/release-notes.md` shall contain the platform matrix of `object.md` §17.1 with a status per row: the JVM Java 8 row `pending` when no Java 8 runtime ran the suite, citing `--release 8` and the animal-sniffer `android-api-level-21` check as compile-time evidence; the Android 5.0, latest Android and Kotlin Android rows `out-of-v1-scope`; and the Servlet row reporting HTTP, multipart, async and SSE tested on an embedded Servlet 3.1 container and WebSocket not supported.
rationale: Covers D-382 and the Platform matrix of object.md §17.1, and wave decisions Release documentation statement (r1 W1-005). Measured (2026-10-20): the build machine has one JDK, OpenJDK 17.0.20 (`java -version`; `/usr/libexec/java_home -V` finds no other), so no Java 8 runtime ran the suite; the bytecode target is Java 8 by `options.release = 8` (CON-BUILD-004). Decision: the Java 8 row status is `pending` until a Java 8 run is recorded, then `verified` with that record as evidence; meanwhile the row cites the two compile-time checks and the command that produced them. The matrix uses the four literals of OPS-REL-003 plus `pending` for a row whose run has not happened. Pitfall: `--release 8` proves the API surface and bytecode level, not runtime behaviour on a Java 8 JVM (for example Java 8 canonical path caching, FR-STATIC-006); the row must say so. Rejected alternative: marking the row `verified` because the bytecode is Java 8; D-382 forbids it.
acceptanceCriteria: `docs/release/release-notes.md` has a platform-matrix table with the five rows of §17.1, a status column using only `verified`, `pending`, `manual-pending` or `out-of-v1-scope`, and the Java 8 row reads `pending` with the sentence that no Java 8 runtime ran, naming `--release 8` and `android-api-level-21` animal-sniffer as compile-time evidence and the JDK that did run (17). [D-382]

The three Android-related rows read `out-of-v1-scope` with the reason `user decision 2026-10-20`; the Servlet row states the embedded container (Jetty 9.4, Servlet 3.1) and the tested scope: HTTP, multipart, async and SSE tested, WebSocket not supported, other containers not tested. [D-382; r1 W1-005; D-363]

A docs test parses the matrix and fails when a row lacks a status literal, when the Java 8 row is `verified` without a recorded Java 8 run reference, or when the file does not mention both compile-time checks. [D-382]

title: How consumers obtain TinyHttpd: includeBuild of the checkout, since this repository does not publish it
requirement: The README and the release documentation shall state that this repository does not publish TinyHttpd, that Gradle `includeBuild` of the TinyHttpd checkout is the one verified way to obtain it, and that the `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` POM dependency on `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd:tinyhttpd-core` and `tinyhttpd-websocket` resolves only when an artifact with those coordinates is available from the consumer's own build of TinyHttpd.
rationale: Covers D-383 and wave decisions TinyHttpd for consumers (r4 W2-002, which supersedes "publish it to mavenLocal themselves" of the Publishing decision). Measured (2026-10-20): TinyHttpd's `build.gradle` sets group `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd` and version `0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` and has no publishing configuration; the checkout is read-only here (I-006, CON-BUILD-010); `settings.gradle` does `includeBuild(tinyHttpdDir)` and warns when the checkout HEAD differs from the verified commit `46b973e` (the checkout was at `38051b6` on this date). Decision: the documented snippet is `includeBuild('/path/to/TinyHttpd')` in the consumer's `settings.gradle`, which substitutes the TinyHttpd coordinates of the POM; the doc states the verified commit. Pitfall: a consumer who depends on `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` from `mavenLocal()` without the included build fails to resolve TinyHttpd; the doc says so, naming the coordinates. Rejected alternative: publishing TinyHttpd to `mavenLocal` from here; the checkout is read-only and has no publishing configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: `README.md` and `docs/release/release-notes.md` each contain the statement that TinyHttpd is not published by this repository, the `includeBuild` snippet for a consumer `settings.gradle`, the two TinyHttpd coordinates with `0.1.0-SNAPSHOT`, and the verified commit `46b973e`, which a docs test asserts. [D-383; r4 W2-002]

A recorded consumer run shows that a Gradle build in a temporary directory that declares `mavenLocal()`, depends on `com.snoworca.naruserve:NaruServe-tinyhttpd:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` and includes the TinyHttpd checkout through `includeBuild` resolves the runtime classpath of the dependency with the TinyHttpd projects, and that the same build without the `includeBuild` fails with an unresolved `tinyhttpd-core`; the run's command, date and results are in the release notes. [D-383]
The documents do not say that TinyHttpd can be taken from `mavenLocal` or a remote repository, and a docs test fails on the phrase "publish it to mavenLocal". [D-383; r4 W2-002]

title: TLS and WSS on the TinyHttpd adapter recorded as a post-v1 item with two reasons

rationale: Covers D-434 and wave decision TLS reason (r1 W1-003, W2-003), which replaces the citation of Q-3's manual device runs.
